items.title: The Nocebo Effect: How Predictions Shape Pain, Behavior, and the AI Era
items.content_text: Many of us are familiar with the placebo — Latin for “I shall please” — an inert or sham treatment with no therapeutic effect on the condition being treated, but is administered as though it were an active treatment. The effect, first documented in the 1940s and 1950s, refers to the beneficial changes that occur as a result of patient expectations, their interaction with the clinician, and the therapeutic context. Expectations alone can influence mood, pain, and even some physiological responses

items.title: Open-sourcing yx_navigation —declarative navigation for Flutter
items.content_text: Navigation in Flutter is a constant string of compromises. At first it looks simple: push and pop. Then the project grows, you add tabs, nested modules, deep links, and one day you wake up to find that every screen opens a little differently and pop() behaves one way over here and another way over there. Navigator 1.0 is simple and predictable, but it falls apart at scale. Navigator 2.0 gives you full control, but the amount of boilerplate is so painful you might as well roll your own framework.
